FINDINGS.md D2 module B (category: fixture AND core). The condition is the module's own id because processCallback() throws a raw RuntimeException ('The user was authenticated on the initial visit to login page. This must not be attempted until the second visit') and AbstractTestModule.handleException logs it under getName(); there is no condition class to cite. Observed cause (fixture): auto-approve issues a code on the FIRST /authorize visit. Latent cause (core): resolve_authorization_request (http.rs) -> validate_pushed_authorization_request (par.rs) -> Storage::take_pushed_authorization_request consumes the request_uri at READ time, before the subject and approval steps, so a second pre-completion visit gets a direct 400 invalid_request_uri even with a deferred-auth fixture. Spec: FAPI 2.0 SP Final s5.3.2.2 NOTE 3 recommends enforcing one-time use 'at the point of authorization, not at the point of loading an authorization page'; RFC 9126 s4 makes one-time use a SHOULD with a MAY for reload duplicates; s7.3 (Request Object Replay) is a SHOULD. Consume-at-read is a deliberate, spec-permitted stricter posture, not a security downgrade and not the suite being wrong. Certification needs BOTH deferring consumption to code issuance AND a first visit that does not authenticate (human-driven per the module's own summary). current-block: Testing if access token was revoked after authorization code reuse (the AS 'should' have revoked the access token)
comment: FINDINGS.md D3 (category: fixture). The module redeems an authorization code, REUSES it, then calls the protected resource with the access token minted on the first redemption and expects a 4xx because the AS 'should' have revoked that token on code reuse. oauth-as DOES revoke it: authorization_code_token (server.rs ~4933) detects the replay and calls Storage::revoke_token_family on the family the code minted (RFC 6749 s4.1.2, RFC 9700 s4.1.1), covered in-crate. The WARNING is logged ONLY because the fixture's protected resource (fapi2_conformance_server.rs protected_resource) validates the access token STATELESSLY -- RFC 9068 JWT signature plus RFC 9449 DPoP binding, no RFC 7662 introspection -- so a token that is still signature-valid and unexpired is accepted until expiry even though its family is revoked at the AS. A self-contained-JWT resource that does not introspect is a legitimate, spec-permitted design; revocation on code reuse is a SHOULD, and the suite logs the missing 4xx at WARNING (callAndContinueOnFailure(..., ConditionResult.WARNING)) and templates it as an expected warning, not a failure. This records the resource's stateless design honestly; it does NOT mask an AS defect. Strings captured from run 35487826596 (head c51be96), module log IYLjk64U3xLG4Zr.
